claim: The oblique in the quantificational use of a great deal of is restricted in number.
evidence_summary: Van Eynde and Kim give a great deal of people in example [60].
finding: Allow a plural oblique in at least some uses. The example leaves pseudopartitive headedness unresolved.
inference: If the oblique requires a singular form, can a plural denote the people quantified over?

evidence.source: Frank Van Eynde & Jong-Bok Kim (2023). Pseudo-partitives in English: An HPSG analysis. English Language & Linguistics 27(2), 271–302.
evidence.passage: §3.3, p. 350. The oblique in the quantificational use of a great deal of is restricted in number.
evidence.example: The article develops a second-noun-headed account and gives a great deal of people in (60), from a 2012 blog in COCA.
evidence.establishes: A lexical restriction can fail regardless of which head analysis wins. The published corpus example bears directly on this claim.
evidence.locator: Alternative headedness analysis. For the narrower oblique-number issue, p. 294 (60).
